meta.scene_summary: We are currently paying billions to teach AI how to lie, while the rest of our infrastructure is held together by terminal color codes and prayer.

cooking.headline: The NSA is paying billions to find out if AI is actually smart or just a really good liar
cooking.summary: The government is dropping billions to stress-test AI models, essentially treating them like a high-stakes group project where they're terrified of the outcome. It's the ultimate 'trust but verify' approach, except the verify part involves a budget that could buy a small country.
cooking.plain_english: The National Security Agency is spending billions of dollars to evaluate the security and reliability of artificial intelligence models.

cooking.headline: Docker is launching cloud sandboxes so your AI agents can break things safely
cooking.summary: Docker is now offering cloud-based sandboxes specifically to keep your rogue AI agents from nuking your local machine. It's essentially a digital playpen for the scripts that keep trying to delete your production database.
cooking.plain_english: Docker has released a service that provides secure, isolated cloud environments for running automated software tasks.

cooking.headline: The Dutch government is migrating to NixOS to escape the Microsoft ecosystem.
cooking.summary: Nothing says 'sovereign computing' like replacing a billion-dollar suite with a declarative package manager that requires a PhD to configure. Good luck to the civil servants trying to explain to HR why their spreadsheet won't open because of a missing flake input.
cooking.plain_english: The Dutch government is developing an alternative to Microsoft software using the NixOS operating system.

cooked.headline: Microsoft realizes that nobody actually wanted an AI therapist in their OS
cooked.summary: Microsoft is officially pivoting away from the personal chatbot race after realizing users mostly just want their software to stop crashing. It turns out that when you force a chatbot into every corner of the UI, you're mostly just building a very expensive paperclip.
cooked.plain_english: Microsoft is redesigning its Copilot software to move away from being a general-purpose personal assistant.

cooked.headline: The Pentagon just put Anthropic on the 'do not trust' list
cooked.summary: Anthropic is building the future of AI, but the U.S. appeals court just labeled them a supply chain risk.

cooked.headline: ASML sold zero machines in Europe and is now asking for a handout
cooked.summary: ASML makes the most complex machines on Earth, yet they somehow managed to sell absolutely nothing to their own neighbors this year. It's the industrial equivalent of building a world-class kitchen and then being surprised when no one in the neighborhood wants to cook.
cooked.plain_english: ASML reported that it did not sell any of its semiconductor manufacturing equipment in Europe during 2026 and is requesting government support to increase regional demand.

cooked.headline: GitLab's status page is the most popular read on the internet today
cooked.summary: GitLab went down, forcing developers to actually talk to their coworkers instead of pushing code. It's the ultimate productivity hack that nobody ever asked for.
cooked.plain_english: The GitLab platform experienced a service outage that prevented users from accessing their repositories and tools.

cooked.headline: Sourcehut got pwned by a terminal color code.
cooked.summary: An XSS vulnerability in a library designed to turn logs into HTML allowed attackers to hijack accounts, proving that even your build logs are out to get you. It's the digital equivalent of tripping over your own shoelaces while trying to win a marathon.
cooked.plain_english: A security vulnerability in a tool used to convert text logs into web pages allowed unauthorized access to user accounts on the Sourcehut platform.

cooked.headline: The antivirus software that needed an antivirus
cooked.summary: Avast built a sandbox to keep malware out, but researchers just found a way to break out of it like it was a prison movie. It turns out the security software meant to protect your PC was actually hosting a secret exit for anyone who knew where to look.
cooked.plain_english: Security researchers discovered a vulnerability in Avast Antivirus that allows malicious software to bypass the program's protective containment environment.

cooked.headline: A $1.1M fine for failing the 'hide your giant gas generators' challenge
cooked.summary: A data center tried to keep their massive collection of gas generators on the down-low, but they forgot that satellites exist in the year 2026. They got hit with a seven-figure fine for emitting more than just heat, proving that your neighbors can see everything from space.
cooked.plain_english: A data center was fined $1.1 million by New Jersey regulators for operating dozens of unpermitted gas generators that were discovered via aerial photography.
